# Affine KKT-row normalization and an exact root-to-volume obstruction
residual-threshold program. It gives an exact projective normalization and
an actual convex cap-cover example in which the proposed uncorrected
root-to-volume implication has the opposite sign. It is not a counterexample
to OC, nor does it rule out an argument using genuinely critical caps at a
below-target deepest point.

## 1. The exact positive affine-row normalization

Let a KKT martingale row have positive source height h_p and normalized row
weights theta_j>0, with

    sum_j theta_j=1,     sum_j theta_j z_j=p.

Suppose every destination height is positive. The supporting-face property
of the audited KKT coupling says that the optimal convex threshold agrees,
on the convex hull B of these destinations, with an affine function

    h(z)=h_p+a.(z-p)>0.

In fact equality with the source's supporting affine function holds at all
destinations; convexity and the supporting inequality then force equality
on their full convex hull. In particular

    sum_j theta_j h_j=h_p.                              (1)

For q>1, all destinations with positive coupling mass automatically have
positive height, since their column mass is q h_j^(q-1). For q=1 this
positivity is an additional hypothesis of this particular normalization.

On the actual convex body restricted to bases in B, set

    z'=(z-p)/h(z),       x'=x/h(z).                      (2)

The base translation in (2) is essential: an unanchored map z/h(z) need not
be injective when the affine denominator has zero constant term. The inverse
of (2) is

    h(z)=h_p/(1-a.z'),
    z=p+h_p z'/(1-a.z'),    x=h_p x'/(1-a.z').           (3)

The denominators are positive on the image. Since h is bounded away from
zero on the compact set B, (2) and (3) are continuous inverse maps there.
The image is a compact convex set. Indeed a convex combination of original
points maps to the convex combination of their images with weights tilted
in proportion to their positive denominators, and conversely one recovers
the original weights by dividing by those denominators and renormalizing.

An original cap

    b.z+u.x>=c

becomes the affine cap

    [b-(b.p-c)a/h_p].z'+u.x'+(b.p-c)/h_p>=0.           (4)

Thus open residual complements, closed caps, and all their finite
intersections are transported exactly. A q-dimensional section volume is
divided by h(z)^q. This remains true for an intrinsic q-volume in a
translated affine plane, because the within-fiber map is scalar dilation;
it is not an assertion about ambient (n+q)-volume.

Set

    eta_j=theta_j h_j/h_p.

Then eta_j>0, sum eta_j=1, and sum eta_j z'_j=0. If the chosen residual
section R_p has root h_p at the source, and every destination residual has
positive q-volume, intrinsic Brunn--Minkowski gives

    1 >= sum_j eta_j r_j,
    r_j=|R_(z_j)|^(1/q)/h_j.                            (5)

Here the residuals are actual convex intersections with the original cap
complements. If their q-direction spaces differed, their positive
Minkowski combination at the actual q-dimensional source would have
dimension greater than q. Hence all relevant direction spaces agree and
ordinary intrinsic BM applies. A zero-volume or empty residual is NOT
silently substituted into (5); that case needs its separate actual-cap
payment or another argument.

The exact conversion back to the original row-weighted residual volume is

    sum_j theta_j |R_(z_j)|
       =h_p sum_j eta_j h_j^(q-1) r_j^q.               (6)

The projective map therefore does not erase the height weights or turn
the first root moment (5) into an upper bound on the volume moment (6).
It also generally sends integer bases to noninteger sites. Convex
incidence and finite Helly numbers are preserved by this bijective
projective map on its positive chart; literal lattice parity is not.

## 2. An actual convex family with an attained constant-height optimum

Fix an integer q>=2 and a parameter 0<a<1. Let

    T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_(q-1),q! e_q),
    ell(x)=x_1+...+x_(q-1)+x_q/q!.

Then |T|=1 and, for 0<=r<=2,

    2T intersect {ell(x)<r} = rT up to its boundary,
    |rT|=r^q.

Take the full-dimensional convex body and its actual mixed set

    C=[-1,1] x 2T,
    S=C intersect (Z x R^q).

Its complete integer base set is {-1,0,1}, all three fiber volumes are
2^q, and its total mixed mass is M=3*2^q. Use the three closed ambient caps

    H_+={ell(x)>=1+a z},
    H_-={ell(x)>=1-a z},
    H_0={ell(x)<=1}.                                   (7)

These caps cover the entire real body C: the union of the first two has
threshold 1-a|z|<=1, while H_0 contains all points of height at most 1.
They are proper caps on every measured fiber. Thus the example has no
empty residual, supporting-plane mass, or lower-dimensional degeneracy.

For the one-cap residual program, the three residual roots at an integer
base z are respectively

    1+a z,     1-a z,     (2^q-1)^(1/q).

Since q>=2, their pointwise minimum is

    (e_-1,e_0,e_1)=(1-a,1,1-a).                        (8)

The unique optimal sampled convex threshold is

    h_-1=h_0=h_1=1,           R=3.                     (9)

To prove this, any feasible threshold has h_0>=1 and
h_-1+h_1>=2h_0. Strict convexity of the qth power gives

    h_-1^q+h_0^q+h_1^q >= 3 h_0^q >=3.

The constant threshold 1 is feasible and attains 3; equality forces all
three heights to equal 1. This establishes optimality and uniqueness
without relying on a numerical convex program.

## 3. An explicit KKT coupling and the strict volume defect

At the optimum let all threshold slopes be zero. The stationarity masses
are s_-1=s_0=s_1=q. Choose the only nonzero inequality multipliers as

    mu_(0,-1)=mu_(0,1)=q.

Their row moment is zero. With

    lambda_0=3q,       lambda_-1=lambda_1=0,

all KKT equations and complementary slackness hold. An explicit compatible
martingale has

    pi_(0,-1)=pi_(0,0)=pi_(0,1)=q,

and all other entries zero. Its normalized source row has destination
weights 1/3 each. Every destination lies on the same strictly positive
affine support face h=1, and the source is a positive obstacle contact.

The cap H_+ is an active minimizing residual at the source. Its residual
roots at the three destinations are (1-a,1,1+a). Therefore (5) is equality:

    [(1-a)+1+(1+a)]/3=1.

But the corresponding residual-volume average is

    [(1-a)^q+1+(1+a)^q]/3
       =1+Delta_q(a)/3 >1,
    Delta_q(a)=(1-a)^q+(1+a)^q-2>0.                    (10)

The strict sign follows directly from strict convexity of t^q on positive
t; for integer q it also follows by expanding the positive even-power
terms. In this example (2) is already the identity, so no projective
renormalization can repair the missing implication.

Equivalently the source captured volume is 2^q-1, whereas the row-average
actual captured volume of the SAME original cap H_+ is

    2^q-1-Delta_q(a)/3 < 2^q-1.                        (11)

Its full actual mixed cap mass is

    mu(H_+)=mu(H_-)=3(2^q-1)-Delta_q(a),
    mu(H_0)=3.                                        (12)

Thus transporting the source's raw own-cap charge to the row destinations
with the normalized KKT weights loses exactly Delta_q(a)/3 in (11).
The already proved maximum-load cap estimate is unaffected; it never
claimed that this transport preserves captured volume.

For the completely rational planar specialization q=2, a=1/2, the
residual roots are (1/2,1,3/2), their squared average is 7/6, and

    M=12, R=3, mu(H_+)=mu(H_-)=17/2, mu(H_0)=3.

The source captured area is 3 and the transported average is 17/6.
All numbers are exact.

## 4. Scope of the obstruction

The example disproves an upper-volume conclusion from a positive affine
row, exact KKT conditions, actual residual BM, and even equality in the
root BM inequality. It also disproves payment of this particular defect
by the original fibers' BM slack alone: all original fibers here are
identical, so their BM comparisons are exact.

It does not disprove OC. The caps (7) are not asserted to be a critical
cover at the body's deepest points or to have mass below gamma_q M/2.
A successful continuation can still use those additional hypotheses, or
retain an exact positive correction for the volume defect (10). The
unconditional projective row argument by itself supplies no such payment.
